board.name: Online Scope Studio Homepage
board.goal: Reposition the current Online Scope Studio homepage from a broad website-development offer into a clear, credible long-term technical-partner story for small-to-medium businesses, while preserving truthful services and an understandable conversion path.
board.audience: Small-to-medium business owners, founders, and marketing or operations leaders who need one accountable technical partner across websites, commerce, custom web applications, automation, measurement, maintenance, and UI/UX.
board.constraints: Use a black, warm-white, and grey foundation with one restrained signal accent. Keep the hero short and balanced. Show business outcomes before tool logos. Preserve real project evidence only. Do not present OSS as a generic agency or public solo-founder business. Do not add social-media marketing. Avoid generic AI-purple styling, glassmorphism, cursor effects, scroll-jacking, fake proof, and decorative 3D. Any motion or 3D must improve comprehension and remain accessible, responsive, and performance-conscious.
unresolvedQuestions: Should the signal accent remain warm orange or move toward restrained blue?
Should fixed starting prices appear on the homepage or remain on a dedicated pricing page?
Which three to four projects have publishable outcomes beyond screenshots?
Does one meaningful 3D or technical visual improve comprehension enough to justify its cost?
Should the audience remain broad across Indian SMBs or narrow toward operations-heavy growth businesses?
Which short phrase communicates long-term technical partnership without outsourced-CTO theatre?

items.rationale: Establish an editorial, studio-quality brand direction without locking the candidate to one layout.
items.note: Inspect short hero typography, project presentation, whitespace, borders, and restrained colour. Treat it as visual research only; it provides no code exports.

items.rationale: Set an upper craft boundary for typography and interaction while making restraint an explicit review criterion.
items.note: Inspect page rhythm and motion timing, then reject continuous spectacle, illegible display type, and agency-showcase excess.

items.rationale: Research hero, services, proof, process, objection, and CTA section patterns for an original homepage structure.
items.note: Retain source URLs. Do not mirror screenshots or paid components; membership and request limits remain provider concerns.

items.rationale: Define a readable display/body hierarchy that feels editorial and premium without sacrificing clarity for non-technical buyers.
items.note: Inspect scale, line length, contrast, and pairing principles. Font licensing and availability must be revalidated before production use.

items.rationale: Ground buttons, navigation, dialogs, and form-adjacent components in accessible, implementable React patterns.
items.note: Use primitives and behaviour, not the default shadcn visual identity. Preserve OSS-specific spacing, type, borders, and colour decisions.

items.rationale: Explore contemporary component-level alternatives and implementation precedents without turning the candidate into a component collage.
items.note: Validate code, dependencies, originality, licensing, and accessibility before reuse. Select only patterns serving the brief.

items.rationale: Implement a small motion system with purposeful entrance, feedback, and reduced-motion behaviour.
items.note: Prefer opacity/transform and short state transitions. No scroll-jacking, continuous motion, or animation used to hide weak hierarchy.

items.rationale: Check whether the restrained accent and neutral palette remain legible across common vision conditions.
items.note: Use it as one contrast-research input, then verify final tokens against WCAG-oriented tooling and manual review.

items.rationale: Challenge the information architecture and section sequence before visual polish begins.
items.note: Use planning and structural principles only. Revalidate access, terms, and any paid-library boundary before using provider material.

items.rationale: Test one bounded technical-visual hypothesis rather than assuming 3D belongs on the page.
items.note: Include only if it explains systems, connection, or technical depth better than static composition. Otherwise record a deliberate rejection.

items.rationale: Reject v0 as the primary visual-authority or taste source for this proof because generated defaults could bias the candidate toward generic AI UI.
items.note: It may be considered later as an implementation assistant only after the brief and research pack control the direction.

items.rationale: Its enterprise product-interface system is not the primary fit for an editorial marketing homepage.
items.note: This is project-specific. Ant Design remains useful for complex application interfaces, not this candidate's brand direction.

items.rationale: Mobile product-flow research is not the highest-priority input for the homepage positioning and section-architecture problem.
items.note: Reopen for a future product onboarding or application-flow task, not for this marketing-page proof.

items.rationale: Recorded app and website flows do not directly solve the homepage's technical-partner positioning and visual-system task.
items.note: Reopen when researching a specific product journey, form flow, onboarding, or conversion sequence.

implementationReminders: Keep the hero headline short enough to remain visually balanced on mobile and desktop.
Do not identify OSS publicly as a solo-founder business.
Do not add social-media marketing to the service scope.
Use only real portfolio evidence; omit unsupported metrics, testimonials, and client-logo claims.
Treat the accent colour and 3D hypothesis as open decisions until the candidate is reviewed.
